newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish fixed bond yields seen flat at tender.
newsitem.headline: Polish fixed bond yields seen flat at tender.

text.p: The average yields of Poland's 16-percent two-year bond and 12-percent five-year bonds are expected to hold flat at Thursday's joint 800 million zloty primary auction, analysts said on Wednesday.

They said foreign investors, which have been absent from recent treasury tenders, were likely to return on Thursday and bid mainly for the attractive two-year bond, which yielded around 19.9 percent at the last auction on August 22.
"The shorter bonds are quite attractive and should generate interest from both domestic and foreign investors," said Krzysztof Kozuchowski, treasury dealer at ING bank in Warsaw. @

Analysts said bond prices were likely to hold relatively flat from the last auction because year-on-year inflation in August was 20.5 percent, a touch above July's 20.4 percent and food prices rose quickly at the start of September.
"Fundementals have not changed since the last auction so bond prices should not be much different on Thursday," said Wojciech Kowalczyk, treasury dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.
At the last auction in late August the treasury sold 600 million zlotys of two-year bonds at an average price of 93.62 and 159 million five-year bonds at an average price of 80.87. @
Analysts said the two-year paper, the most liquid Polish bond, was attractive for foreigners looking to extend the horizon of their investment portfolios.

"The two-year bond is probably the best Polish longer-term paper and foreign investor interest should pick up after recent statements from (Finance Minister Grzegorz) Kolodko and the (International Monetary Fund) IMF," Handlowy's Kowalczyk said. @

The IMF and Kolodko said last week that Poland should consider more flexibility in its exchange rate policy, which the market took as a signal that the zloty's crawling-peg devaluation rate may be cut from the current one percent per month.
Kolodko also said he envisiged a 4.3 percent real-term appreciation of the zloty next year though he did not specify how this would be achieved.
The central bank sets Poland's exchnage rate policy and has said it wants to keep the zloty stable in the long-term.
